chunks: Al-Qasim narrated from Abd al-Samad ibn Bashir, from Mu'awiya who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Verily, keeping ties with relatives makes the accounting easier on the Day of Judgment.'
They maintain the ties that Allah has ordered to be maintained, stand in awe of their Lord, and fear the harshness of reckoning.

key_terms.سُوءَ الْحِسَابِ: Harshness of reckoning / Evil outcome of accounting

ai.seo_question: How does keeping ties with relatives affect the Day of Judgment according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Zuhd*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes *silat al-rahim* not merely as a social virtue but as a spiritual mechanism that mitigates the severity of the final reckoning. By citing Surah al-Ra'd, he connects the physical act of maintaining kinship with the internal state of *khawf* (fear of God), illustrating how familial bonds serve as a tangible expression of divine obedience that eases the soul's transition to the afterlife.
